<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">ALS tends to progress in a linear fashion over time. Thus the overall rate of decline in each patient is fairly constant and predictable, unlike many other non-cancer diseases.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">However, no single variable deteriorates at a uniform rate in all patients. Therefore, multiple clinical parameters are required to judge the progression of ALS.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Although ALS usually presents in a localized anatomical area, the location of initial presentation does not correlate with survival time. By the time patients become end-stage, muscle denervation has become widespread, affecting all areas of the body, and initial predominance patterns do not persist.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Progression of disease differs markedly from patient to patient. Some patients decline rapidly and die quickly; others progress more slowly. For this reason, the history of the rate of progression in individual patients is important to obtain to predict prognosis.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">In end-state ALS, two factors are critical in determining prognosis: ability to breathe, and to a lesser extent ability to swallow. The former can be managed by artificial ventilation, and the latter by gastrostomy or other artificial feeding, unless the patient has recurrent aspiration pneumonia. While not necessarily a contraindication to Hospice care, the decision to institute either artificial ventilation or artificial feeding may significantly alter six month prognosis.</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Examination by a neurologist within three months of assessment for hospice is advised, both to confirm the diagnosis and to assist with prognosis.</li>
</ol>

<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">FVC &lt; 40% predicted (seated or supine) and 2 or more of the following symptoms and/or signs:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Dyspnea at rest;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Orthopnea;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Use of accessory respiratory musculature;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Paradoxical abdominal motion;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Respiratory rate &gt; 20;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Reduced speech / vocal volume;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Weakened cough;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Symptoms of sleep disordered breathing;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Frequent awakening;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Daytime somnolence / excessive daytime sleepiness;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Unexplained headaches;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Unexplained confusion;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Unexplained anxiety;<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />Unexplained nausea.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">If unable to perform the FVC test patients meet this criterion if they manifest 3 or more of the above symptoms/signs.</li>
</ol>
<p><span style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important; white-space: normal; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stage of dementia (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria.</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Patients with dementia should show all the following characteristics:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Stage seven or beyond according to the Functional Assessment Staging Scale;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Unable to ambulate without assistance;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Unable to dress without assistance;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Unable to bathe without assistance;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Urinary and fecal incontinence, intermittent or constant;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">No consistently meaningful verbal communication: stereotypical phrases only or the ability to speak is limited to six or fewer intelligible words.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Patients should have had one of the following within the past 12 months:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Aspiration pneumonia;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Pyelonephritis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Septicemia;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Decubitus ulcers, multiple, stage 3-4;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Fever, recurrent after antibiotics;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Inability to maintain sufficient fluid and calorie intake with 10% weight loss during the previous six months or serum albumin &lt; 2.5 gm/dl.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Heart Disease</strong><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; white-space: normal; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stage of heart disease (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria. (1 and 2 should be present. Factors from 3 will add supporting documentation.)</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">At the time of initial certification or recertification for hospice, the patient is or has been already optimally treated for heart disease, or are patients who are either not candidates for surgical procedures or who decline those procedures. (Optimally treated means that patients who are not on vasodilators have a medical reason for refusing these drugs, e.g., hypotension or renal disease.)<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Patients with congestive heart failure or angina should meet the criteria for the New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV. (Class IV patients with heart disease have an inability to carry on any physical activity. Symptoms of heart failure or of the anginal syndrome may be present even at rest. If any physical activity is undertaken, discomfort is increased.) Significant congestive heart failure may be documented by an ejection fraction of less than or equal to 20%, but is not required if not already available.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of the following factors will support but is not required to establish eligibility for hospice care:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Treatment-resistant symptomatic supraventricular or ventricular arrhythmias;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">History of cardiac arrest or resuscitation;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">History of unexplained syncope;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Brain embolism of cardiac origin;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Concomitant HIV disease.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: bold; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">HIV Disease</strong><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><span style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important; white-space: normal; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stage of their illness (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria. (1 and 2 should be present; factors from 3 will add supporting documentation.)</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">CD4+ Count &lt; 25 cells/mcl or persistent (2 or more assays at least one month apart) viral load &gt;100,000 copies/ml, plus one of the following:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">CNS lymphoma;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Untreated, or persistent despite treatment, wasting (loss of at least 10% lean body mass);</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) bacteremia, untreated, unresponsive to treatment, or treatment refused;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Systemic lymphoma, with advanced HIV disease and partial response to chemotherapy;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Visceral Kaposi&rsquo;s sarcoma unresponsive to therapy;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Renal failure in the absence of dialysis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Cryptosporidium infection;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Toxoplasmosis, unresponsive to therapy.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Decreased performance status, as measured by the Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) scale, of less than or equal to 50%.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of the following factors will support eligibility for hospice care:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Chronic persistent diarrhea for one year;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Persistent serum albumin &lt; 2.5;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Concomitant, active substance abuse;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Age &gt; 50 years;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Absence of or resistance to effective antiretroviral, chemotherapeutic and prophylactic drug therapy related specifically to HIV disease;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Advanced AIDS dementia complex;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Toxoplasmosis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Congestive heart failure, symptomatic at rest;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Advanced liver disease.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: bold; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Liver Disease</strong><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><br style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;" /><span style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important; white-space: normal; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stage of liver disease (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria. (1 and 2 should be present, factors from 3 will lend supporting documentation.)</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">The patient should show both a and b:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Prothrombin time prolonged more than 5 seconds over control, or International Normalized Ratio (INR) &gt; 1.5;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Serum albumin &lt; 2.5 gm/dl.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">End stage liver disease is present and the patient shows at least one of the following:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Ascites, refractory to treatment or patient non-compliant;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hepatorenal syndrome (elevated creatinine and BUN with oliguria (&lt; 400 ml/day) and urine sodium concentration &lt; 10 mEq/l);</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hepatic encephalopathy, refractory to treatment, or patient non-compliant;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Recurrent variceal bleeding, despite intensive therapy.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of the following factors will support eligibility for hospice care:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Progressive malnutrition;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Muscle wasting with reduced strength and endurance;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Continued active alcoholism (&gt; 80 gm ethanol/day);</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hepatocellular carcinoma;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">HBsAg (Hepatitis B) positivity;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hepatitis C refractory to interferon treatment.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stage of pulmonary disease (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria. The criteria refer to patients with various forms of advanced pulmonary disease who eventually follow a final common pathway for end stage pulmonary disease. (1 and 2 should be present. Documentation of 3, 4, and 5, will lend supporting documentation.)</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Severe chronic lung disease as documented by both a and b:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Disabling dyspnea at rest, poorly or unresponsive to bronchodilators, resulting in decreased functional capacity, e.g., bed to chair existence, fatigue, and cough; (Documentation of Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second (FEV1), after bronchodilator, less than 30% of predicted is objective evidence for disabling dyspnea, but is not necessary to obtain.)</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Progression of end stage pulmonary disease, as evidenced by increasing visits to the emergency department or hospitalizations for pulmonary infections and/or respiratory failure or increasing physician home visits prior to initial certification. (Documentation of serial decrease of FEV1&gt;40 ml/year is objective evidence for disease progression, but is not necessary to obtain.)</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hypoxemia at rest on room air, as evidenced by pO2 less than or equal to 55 mmHg, or oxygen saturation less than or equal to 88%, determined either by arterial blood gases or oxygen saturation monitors, (these values may be obtained from recent hospital records) OR hypercapnia, as evidenced by pCO2 greater than or equal to 50 mmHg. (This value may be obtained from recent [within 3 months] hospital records.)<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Right heart failure (RHF) secondary to pulmonary disease (Cor pulmonale) (e.g., not secondary to left heart disease or valvulopathy).<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Unintentional progressive weight loss of greater than 10% of body weight over the preceding six months.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Resting tachycardia &gt; 100/min.</li>
</ol>

Factors from 5 will lend supporting documentation.)</span></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">The patient is not seeking dialysis or renal transplant, or is discontinuing dialysis. As with any other condition, an individual with renal disease is eligible for the Hospice benefit if that individual has a prognosis of six months or less, if the illness runs its normal course. There is no regulation precluding patients on dialysis from electing Hospice care. However, the continuation of dialysis will significantly alter a patient&rsquo;s prognosis, and thus potentially impact that individual&rsquo;s eligibility.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />When an individual elects Hospice care for end stage renal disease (ESRD) or for a condition to which the need for dialysis is related, the Hospice agency is financially responsible for the dialysis. In such cases, there is no additional reimbursement beyond the per diem rate. The only situation in which a beneficiary may access both the Hospice benefit and the ESRD benefit is when the need for dialysis is not related to the patient&rsquo;s terminal illness.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Creatinine clearance &lt; 10 cc/min (&lt;15 cc/min. for diabetics); or &lt; 15cc/min (&lt; 20cc/min for diabetics) with comorbidity of congestive heart failure.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Serum creatinine &gt; 8.0 mg/dl (&gt;6.0 mg/dl for diabetics).<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) &lt;10 ml/min.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Comorbid conditions:
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Mechanical ventilation;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Malignancy (other organ system);</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Chronic lung disease;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Advanced cardiac disease;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Advanced liver disease;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Immunosuppression/AIDS;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Albumin &lt; 3.5 gm/dl;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Platelet count &lt; 25,000;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Disseminated intravascular coagulation;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Gastrointestinal bleeding.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: bold; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Chronic Kidney Disease</strong><span style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; word-spacing: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important; white-space: normal; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"> (1 and either 2, 3 or 4 should be present. <ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">The patient is not seeking dialysis or renal transplant, or is discontinuing dialysis; As with any other condition, an individual with renal disease is eligible for the Hospice benefit if that individual has a prognosis of six months or less, if the illness runs its normal course. There is no regulation precluding patients on dialysis from electing Hospice care. However, the continuation of dialysis will significantly alter a patient&rsquo;s prognosis, and thus potentially impact that individual&rsquo;s eligibility.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />When an individual elects Hospice care for end stage renal disease (ESRD) or for a condition to which the need for dialysis is related, the Hospice agency is financially responsible for the dialysis. In such cases, there is no additional reimbursement beyond the per diem rate. The only situation in which a beneficiary may access both the hospice benefit and the ESRD benefit is when the need for dialysis is not related to the patient&rsquo;s terminal illness.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Creatinine clearance &lt;10 cc/min (&lt; 15 cc/min for diabetics); or &lt; 15cc/min (&lt; 20cc/min for diabetics) with comorbidity of congestive heart failure.<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Serum creatinine &gt; 8.0 mg/dl (&gt;6.0 mg/dl for diabetics).<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Signs and symptoms of renal failure:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Uremia;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Oliguria (&lt; 400 cc/24 hours);</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Intractable hyperkalemia (&gt; 7.0) not responsive to treatment;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Uremic pericarditis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Hepatorenal syndrome;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Intractable fluid overload, not responsive to treatment.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) &lt;10 ml/min.</li>
</ol>

font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Patients will be considered to be in the terminal stages of stroke or coma (life expectancy of six months or less) if they meet the following criteria:</span><br style="text-align: left; <ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) or Palliative Performance Scale (PPS) of &lt; 40% .<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Inability to maintain hydration and caloric intake with one of the following:
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Weight loss &gt; 10% in the last 6 months or &gt; 7.5% in the last 3 months;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Serum albumin &lt; 2.5 gm/dl;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Current history of pulmonary aspiration not responsive to speech language pathology intervention; Sequential calorie counts documenting inadequate caloric/fluid intake;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Dysphagia severe enough to prevent patient from continuing fluids/foods necessary to sustain life and patient does not receive artificial nutrition and hydration.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: bold; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Coma (any etiology):</strong></p>
<ol style="text-align: left; color: #333333; text-transform: none; text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: normal; font-family: Verdana, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 10px; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; box-sizing: border-box; orphans: 2; widows: 2; background-color: #ffffff; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Comatose patients with any 3 of the following on day three of coma:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">abnormal brain stem response;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">absent verbal response;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">absent withdrawal response to pain;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">serum creatinine &gt; 1.5 mg/dl.</li>
</ol>
</ol>
<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /><br style="box-sizing: border-box;" /></li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of the following factors will support eligibility for hospice care:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of medical complications, in the context of progressive clinical decline, within the previous 12 months, which support a terminal prognosis:
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Aspiration pneumonia;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Pyelonephritis;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Refractory stage 3-4 decubitus ulcers;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Fever recurrent after antibiotics.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Documentation of diagnostic imaging factors which support poor prognosis after stroke include:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">For non-traumatic hemorrhagic stroke:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Large-volume hemorrhage on CT:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;" type="a">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Infratentorial: greater than or equal to 20 ml.;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Supratentorial: greater than or equal to 50 ml.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Ventricular extension of hemorrhage;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Surface area of involvement of hemorrhage greater than or equal to 30% of cerebrum;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Midline shift greater than or equal to 1.5 cm.;</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Obstructive hydrocephalus in patient who declines, or is not a candidate for, ventriculoperitoneal shunt.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">For thrombotic/embolic stroke:<br style="box-sizing: border-box;" />
<ol style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; box-sizing: border-box;">
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Large anterior infarcts with both cortical and subcortical involvement</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Large bihemispheric infarcts</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Basilar artery occlusion</li>
<li style="box-sizing: border-box;">Bilateral vertebral artery occlusion.</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>The guidelines contained in this policy are intended to help providers determine when patients are appropriate for the Medicare Hospice benefit. As each patient is unique, there are patients for whom a particular guideline does not match. In such cases, it is important for providers to meticulously document the factors which specify the individual&rsquo;s terminal prognosis.<br /><br />There are also patients who match a guideline at the start of hospice care, and who continue to do so for a prolonged period, e.g., greater than six months. While it is true that there is not a strict six month limit on the Hospice benefit, the underlying precept is that the beneficiary must have a prognosis of six months or less, if the illness runs its normal course. A beneficiary may match a guideline, but by virtue of that individual having lived for a significantly prolonged period thereafter, he/she has shown that guideline to be inadequate to predict the appropriate terminal prognosis.<br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /></strong><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">ACC/AHA Guidelines for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Heart Failure in the Adult: Executive Summary A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Practice Guidelines (Committee to Revise the 1995 Guidelines for the Evaluation and Management of Heart Failure)<br /><br />Stages of Heart Failure (HF)<br /><br />Stage A</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Patients at high risk of developing HF because of the presence of conditions that are strongly associated with the development of HF. Such patients have no identified structural or functional abnormalities of the pericardium, myocardium, or cardiac valves and have never shown signs or symptoms of HF.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Example:</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Systemic hypertension; coronary artery disease; diabetes mellitus; history of cardiotoxic drug therapy or alcohol abuse; personal history of rheumatic fever; family history of cardiomyopathy.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Stage B</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Patients who have developed structural heart disease that is strongly associated with the development of HF but who have never show signs or symptoms of HF.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Example:</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Left ventricular hypertrophy or fibrosis; left ventricular dilatation or hypocontractility; asymptomatic valvular heart disease; previous myocardial infarction.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Stage C</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Patients who have current or prior symptoms of HF associated with underlying structural heart disease.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Example:</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Dyspnea or fatigue due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction; asymptomatic patients who are undergoing treatment for prior symptoms of HF.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Stage D</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Patients with advanced structural heart disease and marked symptoms of HF at rest despite maximal medical therapy and who require specialized interventions.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Example:</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">Patients who are frequently hospitalized for HF or cannot be safely discharged from the hospital; patients in the hospital awaiting heart transplantation; patients at home receiving continuous intravenous support for symptom relief or being supported with a mechanical circulatory assist device; patients in a hospice setting for management of HF.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Karnofsky Performance Scale (KPS)<br /><br />The Karnofsky Performance Scale Index allows patients to be classified as to their functional impairment. This can be used to compare effectiveness of different therapies and to assess the prognosis in individual patients. The lower the Karnofsky score, the worse the survival for most serious illnesses.<br /><br />KARNOFSKY PERFORMANCE STATUS SCALE DEFINITIONS RATING (%) CRITERIA</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /></p>

<p><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">NYHA Functional Classification for Congestive Heart Failure</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">The New York Heart Association (NYHA) Functional Classification provides a simple way of classifying heart disease (originally cardiac failure). It places patients in one of four categories, based on how much they are limited during physical activity:</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Class I:</strong></strong><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;"> patients with no limitation of activities; they suffer no symptoms from ordinary activities.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Class II:</strong></strong><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;"> patients with slight, mild limitation of activity; they are comfortable with rest or with mild exertion.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Class III:</strong></strong><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;"> patients with marked limitation of activity; they are comfortable only at rest.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Class IV:</strong></strong><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;"> patients who should be at complete rest, confined to bed or chair; any physical activity brings on discomfort and symptoms occur at rest.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><strong><strong style="text-align: left; background-color: #ffffff;">Palliative Performance Scale</strong></strong><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><span style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;">The Palliative Performance Scale (PPS) is a modification of the Karnofsky Performance Scale intended for evaluating patients requiring palliative care. The score can help determine which patients can be managed in the home and which should be admitted to a hospice unit. It was developed in British Columbia, Canada.</span><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /><br style="text-align: left; font-weight: 400; background-color: #ffffff;" /></p>

<table style="width: 420pt; text-align: left; font-weight: 400; border-collapse: collapse; background-color: #ffffff;" border="1" width="700" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="0">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="background: #ffff80; padding: 0.75pt;">
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong><em>The Stages of Alzheimer's Disease</em></strong></p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">
<table style="width: 556px; border-collapse: collapse; background-color: transparent;" border="0" width="100%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tbody>
<tr style="height: 7.8pt;">
<td style="padding: 0in; width: 556px; height: 7.8pt;" width="100%">At the New York University Medical Center's Aging and Dementia Research Center, Barry Reisberg, MD and colleagues have developed the Functional Assessment Staging (FAST) scale, which allows professionals and caregivers to chart the decline of people with Alzheimer's disease. The FAST scale has 16 stages and sub-stages:<br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br />
<table style="width: 5.2in; border-collapse: collapse; background-color: transparent;" border="1" width="624" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="0">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><strong>FAST Scale Stage</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><strong>Characteristics</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">1... normal adult</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">No functional decline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">2... normal older adult</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Personal awareness of some functional decline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">3... early Alzheimer's disease</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Noticeable deficits in demanding job situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">4... mild Alzheimer's</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Requires assistance in complicated tasks such as handling finances, planning parties,etc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">5... moderate Alzheimer's</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Requires assistance in choosing proper attire.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">6... moderately severe Alzheimer's</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Requires assistance dressing, bathing, and toileting. Experiences urinary and fecal incontinence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">7... severe Alzheimer's</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Speech ability declines to about a half-dozen intelligible words. Progressive loss of abilities to walk, sit up, smile, and hold head up.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Detailed Description of Each of the 7 Stages</strong><br /><br /></p>
<p><strong>Stage 1</strong><br />No cognitive decline. No subjective complaints of memory deficit. No memory deficit evident on clinical interviews.</p>
<p><strong>Stage2 (Forgetfulness)</strong><br />Very mild cognitive decline.</p>
<p>Subjective complaints of memory deficit, most frequently in the following area:</p>
<ol start="1" type="a">
<li>forgetting where one has placed familiar objects;</li>
<li>forgetting names on formerly knew well.</li>
</ol>
<p>No objective evidence of memory deficit on clinical interview. No objective deficits in employment or social situations. Appropriate concern regarding symptoms.</p>
<p><strong>Stage 3 (Early Confusional)</strong><br />Mild cognitive decline. Earliest clear-cut deficits.</p>
<p>Manifestations in more than one of the following areas:</p>
<ol start="1" type="a">
<li>patient may have gotten lost when traveling to an unfamiliar location;</li>
<li>co-workers become aware of patient's relatively low performance;</li>
<li>word and name finding deficit becomes evident to intimates;</li>
<li>patient may read a passage of a book and retain relatively little material;</li>
<li>patient may demonstrate decreased facility in remembering names upon introduction to new people;</li>
<li>patient may have lost or misplaced an object of value;</li>
<li>concentration deficit may be evident on clinical testing.</li>
</ol>
<p>Objective evidence of memory deficit obtained only with an intensive interview. Denial begins to become manifest in patient. Mild to moderate anxiety accompanies symptoms.</p>
<p><strong>Stage 4 (Late Confusional)</strong>Moderate cognitive decline. Clear-cut deficit on careful clinical interview.</p>
<p>Deficit manifest in following areas:</p>
<ol start="1" type="a">
<li>decreased knowledge of current and recent events;</li>
<li>may exhibit some deficit in memory of one's personal history;</li>
<li>concentration deficit elicited on serial subtractions;</li>
<li>decreased ability to travel, handle finances, etc.</li>
</ol>
<p>Frequently no deficit in the following areas:</p>
<ol start="1" type="a">
<li>orientation to time and person;</li>
<li>recognition of familiar persons and faces;</li>
<li>ability to travel to familiar locations.</li>
</ol>
<p>Inability to perform complex tasks. Denial is dominant defense mechanism. Flattening of affect and withdrawal from challenging situations occur.</p>
<p><strong>Stage 5 (Early Dementia)</strong> Moderately severe cognitive decline.</p>
<p>Patient can no longer survive without some assistance. Patient is unable during interview to recall a major relevant aspect of their current lives, e.g., an address or telephone number of many<br />years, the names of close family members (such as grandchildren), the name of the high school or college from which they graduated. Frequently some disorientation to time (date, day of week, season, etc.) or to place. An educated person may have difficulty counting back from 40 by 4s or from 20 by 2s. Persons at this stage retain knowledge of many major facts regarding themselves and others. They invariably know their own names and generally know their spouse's and children's names. They require no assistance with toileting and eating, but may have some difficulty choosing the proper clothing to wear.</p>
<p><strong>Stage 6 (Middle Dementia)</strong> Severe cognitive decline.<br /><br />May occasionally forget the name of the spouse upon whom they are entirely dependent for survival. Will be largely unaware of all recent events and experiences in their lives. Retain some knowledge of their past lives but this is very sketchy. Generally unaware of their surroundings, the year, the season, etc. May have difficulty counting from 10, both backward and sometimes forward. Will require some assistance with activities of daily living, e.g., may become incontinent, will require travel assistance but occasionally will display ability to familiar locations. Diurnal rhythm frequently disturbed. Almost always recall their own name. Frequently continue to be able to distinguish familiar from unfamiliar persons in their environment.</p>
<p>Personality and emotional changes occur. These are quite variable and include:</p>
<ol start="1" type="a">
<li>delusional behavior, e.g., patients may accuse their spouse of being an impostor, may talk to imaginary figures in the environment, or to their own reflection in the mirror;</li>
<li>obsessive symptoms, e.g., person may continually repeat simple cleaning activities;</li>
<li>anxiety agitation, and even previously nonexistent violent behavior may occur;</li>
<li>cognitive abulia, i.e., loss of willpower because an individual cannot carry a thought long enough to determine a purposeful course of action.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Stage 7 (Late Dementia)</strong> Very severe cognitive decline. All verbal abilities are lost.</p>
<p>Frequently there is no speech at all - only grunting. Incontinent of urine, requires assistance toileting and feeding. Lose basic psychomotor skills, e.g., ability to walk, sitting and head control. The brain appears to no longer be able to tell the body what to do. Generalized and cortical neurologic signs and symptoms are frequently present.</p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><strong><br />Dr Reisberg has also shown that the decline typical of Alzheimer's disease is the flip side of normal skill acquisition by infants, children, and young adults:</strong></p>
<strong><br /><br /><br /></strong>
<table style="background: white; width: 5.2in; border-collapse: collapse;" border="1" width="624" cellspacing="3" cellpadding="0">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><strong>Ability</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><strong>Age of acquisition during normal development</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><strong><br />Alzheimer's stage at which ability is lost</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><br />Hold a job. Function independently in the world.</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;"><br />12 years and older</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">3... early Alzheimer's disease</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Handle simple finances.</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">8-12 years</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">4... mild Alzheimer's</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">Select proper clothing.</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">5-7 years</td>
<td style="padding: 0.75pt;">5... moderate Alzheimer's</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
</td>
</tr>

title: MolDX: HLA-DQB1*06:02 Testing for Narcolepsy
contractor_name_type:
WPS Insurance Corporation
(MAC - Part A, MAC - Part B)
indication: <p><strong>Indications and Limitations of Coverage</strong><br />Based upon currently available information, HLA-DQB1*06:02 typing (81383) for the diagnosis or management of narcolepsy is considered experimental/investigational/unproven for all populations. Although research suggests a strong association between HLA-DQB1*06:02 and narcolepsy risk, HLA-DQB1*06:02 typing is insufficient to confirm a diagnosis of narcolepsy, rule out a diagnosis of narcolepsy or quantify risk for narcolepsy. Therefore, at this time there is no clinical utility for genetic testing or HLA-DQB1*06:02 typing in the diagnosis or treatment of narcolepsy.<br /><br /><strong>Background</strong><br />Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy (sudden loss of voluntary muscle tone), and uncontrollable sleep episodes. Most cases of narcolepsy are sporadic, with symptoms beginning around the time of adolescence.<br /><br />According to the International Classification of Sleep Disorders, Third Edition (ICSD-3) and the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorder, Fifth Edition (DSM-5), narcolepsy is diagnosed by a combination of physical exam, medical history, polysomnogram, multiple sleep latency testing (MSLT), and low CSF hypocretin-1 levels. Current recommended treatment options include stimulants and antidepressants. At this time, treatment is aimed towards the control of symptoms and is not curative.<sup>12</sup><br /><br />Narcolepsy has a multifactorial etiology, likely caused by the interaction between genetic risk factors and environmental exposures. Research efforts to identify the genetic contributors to narcolepsy have focused on an association between certain human leukocyte antigen (HLA) haplotypes and narcolepsy risk. The HLA complex encodes greater than 200 genes responsible for the recognition of foreign antigens. These genes are highly polymorphic, and certain alleles have long been known to confer risk for autoimmune disorders.<br /><br />A variation of the HLA-DQB1 gene called HLA-DQB1*06:02 has been strongly associated with narcolepsy, particularly in individuals who also have cataplexy and a loss of hypocretins. Several genetic association studies in ethnically diverse populations have found a robust association between narcolepsy and the HLA-DQB1*06:02 allele. However, 15 to 25% of unaffected individuals in the general population also carry this risk haplotype, suggesting that it is necessary but not sufficient for the development of narcolepsy.<sup>6</sup> Additionally, persons with narcolepsy and cataplexy have been identified without the HLA-DQB1*06:02 marker.<sup>4</sup> More recent studies further suggest that predisposition to narcolepsy may be the result of complex genetic associations between multiple risk alleles.<sup>11</sup><br /><br />Despite multiple studies replicating the association between HLA-DQB1*06:02 and narcolepsy in different ethnic groups, the overall contribution of HLA variation to disease risk is low. Monozygotic twin studies have shown only partial concordance (25-31%), indicating that environmental factors play a large role in the etiology of narcolepsy.<sup>8</sup> Recent studies have suggested that exposure to streptococcus, H1N1, and the H1N1 vaccine may also increase the risk for narcolepsy, specifically among individuals with the HLA-DQB1*06:02 allele.<sup>3,14,4</sup><br /><br />Although research suggests a strong association between HLA-DQB1*06:02 and narcolepsy risk, at this time there is no evidence for any diagnostic utility of HLA typing.<sup>5</sup></p>

title: CT of the Head
contractor_name_type:
Palmetto GBA
(MAC - Part A, MAC - Part B)
cms_cov_policy: <p>Title XVIII of the Social Security Act, &sect;1862(a)(1)(A) allows coverage and payment for only those services that are considered to be reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of illness or injury or to improve the functioning of a malformed body member.<br /><br />42 CFR &sect;410.32(a)(b) Diagnostic x-ray tests, diagnostic laboratory tests, and other diagnostic tests: Conditions<br /><br />CMS Internet-Only Manual, Pub. 100-03, Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCD) Manual, Chapter 1, Part 4, &sect;220.1 Computed Tomography (CT)</p>
indication: <p>A cranial computerized tomographic (CT) scan is a very useful and informative neurodiagnostic tool. Scanning of the head in successive layers by a narrow beam of x-rays enables the transmission of x-ray photons in each layer to be measured. A computer is used to process the accumulated x-ray photon data and constructs a graphic image of a tomographic slice. Normal intracranial structures and a wide variety of intracranial disorders may be demonstrated. A cranial CT scan may be ordered without contrast, with injection of standard roentgenographic contrast material or without contrast material, followed by contrast material and further sections. Contrast administration is not without risk to the patient and for some conditions adds little or no benefit to the examination.<br /><br />Cranial CT scans are determined to be reasonable and necessary and are a covered service when the patient has clinical evidence of an intracranial disorder or an established intracranial disorder or disease. The general indications for use of contrast CT scanning are:<br /><br />1. To assess perfusion (e.g., cerebrovascular accident [CVA])<br /><br />2. To characterize a specific lesion<br /><br />3. To detect defects in blood/brain barrier (e.g., infarcts, tumors, infection, vasculitis)<br /><br />4. To detect neovascularity (tumors); or<br /><br />5. For staging of known lung cancer, breast cancer, and lymphomas which are likely to metastasize early to the brain</p>
